entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Girolamo Mazzola Bedoli was a renowned Italian painter active in the Mannerist style from 1525 to 1569. His works, characterized by intricate details and use of chiaroscuro, were highly sought after by European aristocracy during the Renaissance era.

Bedoli's artistic career spanned several continents, with notable commissions in Italy, France, and the Holy Roman Empire. His most celebrated piece, 'The Passion of Christ,' was completed in 1565 for the Benedictine monastery in Saint-Pierre-du-Mont, Normandy.

As a member of the Mannerist movement, Bedoli's work played a significant role in shaping the artistic landscape of the 16th century. His influence can be seen in the works of later artists, including Caravaggio and Rembrandt.

The Mannerist style, which emphasized dramatic lighting and intense emotions, was a response to the realism of the High Renaissance. Bedoli's innovative approach helped pave the way for the Baroque movement, which would dominate European art for centuries to come.
